1	"""Playing a recorded generation back, so a reviewer with no key sees the real thing.
2	
3	Somebody clones this repository, starts it, opens the browser — and has no reason
4	to spend money on a model key. Everything this prototype is judged on lives past
5	that point: a map drawing itself claim by claim, the rules refusing the model in
6	public, a step changed and the trades moving.
7	
8	**Replay puts all of it in front of them**, through the same route, the same
9	stream and the same canvas the live path uses. The only substitution anywhere is
10	where the bytes came from, and the screen says so.
11	
12	The file
13	--------
14	`backend/recordings/<example>.jsonl` — one JSON object per line, no surrounding
15	array and no commas between lines, so a file can be written a line at a time
16	while a run is still going, read a line at a time without holding it all in
17	memory, and read as text in a diff.
18	
19	**Line one is the header; every line after it is one event.** They are told apart
20	by one thing: an event line has an `event` key and the header does not. An event
21	line carries exactly the two fields the wire carries, so the replayer writes them
22	straight out without re-deriving anything — which is what makes "a recording is
23	the stream, line for line" literally true rather than nearly true.
24	
25	Two events are not re-emitted from the file
26	--------------------------------------------
27	**The receipt is rebuilt.** A replay made no calls, so it says exactly that: zero
28	calls, zero tokens, zero searches, zero dollars, the header's date and prompt
29	fingerprint, and `mode: "replay"`. The whole tally is zeroed together rather than
30	the dollars alone — a receipt showing tokens with no dollars would contradict its
31	own price table. The model is copied from the recorded receipt, because the
32	reader is entitled to know which model wrote this map, and the seconds are this
33	replay's own clock.
34	
35	**The likelihoods are recomputed, and therefore never stored.** The header
36	carries the seed, the accepted proposals carry the map, and the rules layer does
37	the rest. So a recording holds no world at all: the files stay small, and replay
38	and live agree by construction rather than by care. Store the numbers instead and
39	the day propagation changes, the demo shows numbers the engine no longer
40	produces and nothing goes red.
41	
42	What this file must never do
43	----------------------------
44	- Never write a recording. `make record-demo` is the only writer, and a
45	  hand-edited file is a piece of state that traces to nobody.
46	- Never guess which recording to play. The match is the person's own sentence,
47	  exact after trimming — playing the Hormuz map back at somebody who asked about
48	  photonic chips is worse than saying no, and afterwards it is indistinguishable
49	  from the product working.
50	- Never let the pacing change an event, an order or a number. It is cosmetic.
51	- Never honour a seed from the request. The header's seed is the one the recorded
52	  run had, and the numbers are recomputed from it.
53	"""
54	
55	import json
56	from collections.abc import Iterator
57	from datetime import date
58	from pathlib import Path
59	from typing import Any
60	
61	from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, ValidationError
62	
63	from katalyst.domain import Graph, Insert, Link, Proposition, propagate
64	from katalyst.engine import events
65	from katalyst.engine.events import (
66	    BeliefsPropagated,
67	    Event,
68	    GenerationStarted,
69	    ProposalAccepted,
70	    Receipt,
71	)
72	from katalyst.settings import get_settings
73	
74	RECORDINGS = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / "recordings"
75	"""Where the committed recordings live when nothing says otherwise.
76	
77	`backend/recordings/`. The settings can point somewhere else — which is what lets
78	a test, and the one browser test that drives both halves, run against a folder of
79	their own without touching the committed one.
80	"""
81	
82	
83	def where_they_live() -> Path:
84	    """Where this running program reads its recordings from.
85	
86	    Read when asked rather than when this module was written, so that pointing a
87	    program at another folder is a setting and not a patch.
88	
89	    Returns:
90	        The folder, from the settings when they name one and `backend/recordings/`
91	        when they do not.
92	    """
93	    said = get_settings().KATALYST_RECORDINGS
94	    return Path(said) if said else RECORDINGS
95	
96	
97	A_COMFORTABLE_PACE = 0.6
98	"""Seconds between events when a recording is played at human speed.
99	
100	Cosmetic and nothing else: it never changes an event, an order or a number. The
101	figure is chosen against a measurement rather than taste — a live proposal took
102	about a minute to come back on the first five recorded calls, so a replay that
103	raced would teach a reviewer that the product is faster than it is, and one that
104	matched would be unwatchable. This is the slowest speed somebody will sit through
105	and the fastest that still reads as *arriving* rather than *appearing*.
106	"""
107	
108	
109	class RecordedInsert(BaseModel):
110	    """The single scripted "…but X happens" a keyless reviewer can make on this map."""
111	
112	    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)
113	
114	    claim_in_words: str = Field(description="What the card offers, word for word.")
115	    answer: Insert = Field(
116	        description="The claim and its arrows, drafted live when the recording was made."
117	    )
118	
119	
120	class RecordingHeader(BaseModel):
121	    """The first line of a recording: everything that is true of the whole file.
122	
123	    It must never carry a likelihood, a range or a world. Numbers are recomputed
124	    from the seed, and a number stored here could one day disagree with the engine
125	    that is running.
126	    """
127	
128	    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)
129	
130	    base_id: str = Field(
131	        description=(
132	            "The identifier of the map this recording builds, minted when the "
133	            "recording was made. Emphatically not the word `hormuz`: the file is "
134	            "named for the launchpad card, and the map inside carries a minted "
135	            "identifier so it can never be confused with the hand-written stored "
136	            "example that already answers to that name."
137	        )
138	    )
139	    seed: int = Field(description="The one number the rules layer re-propagates with.")
140	    recording_date: date = Field(description="The day `make record-demo` wrote this file.")
141	    prompt_hash: str = Field(description="The fingerprint of the prompt the run was made against.")
142	    insert: RecordedInsert = Field(
143	        description="The one scripted intervention this recording can answer."
144	    )
145	
146	
147	class RecordingSummary(BaseModel):
148	    """One recording the first screen can offer, and when it was made."""
149	
150	    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)
151	
152	    example: str = Field(description="The short name of the example, matching its file name.")
153	    recording_date: date = Field(description="The day `make record-demo` wrote it.")
154	
155	
156	class Recording(BaseModel):
157	    """One whole recorded generation: its header and its events, in order."""
158	
159	    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)
160	
161	    example: str = Field(description="The short name of the example, from the file's own name.")
162	    header: RecordingHeader = Field(description="Everything true of the whole file.")
163	    lines: tuple[tuple[str, dict[str, Any]], ...] = Field(
164	        description="Every event after the header, as the name it travels under and its payload."
165	    )
166	
167	    @property
168	    def hypothesis(self) -> str:
169	        """The sentence this recording was made from, read off its own first event."""
170	        for name, payload in self.lines:
171	            if name == events.NAMES[GenerationStarted]:
172	                return str(payload.get("hypothesis", ""))
173	        return ""
174	
175	
176	def read(path: Path) -> Recording:
177	    """Read one recording off disk.
178	
179	    Args:
180	        path: The file to read.
181	
182	    Returns:
183	        Its header and its events, in the order they were written.
184	
185	    Raises:
186	        ValueError: If the file is empty, or its first line is not a header.
187	    """
188	    written = [one for one in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines() if one.strip()]
189	    if not written:
190	        raise ValueError(f"{path.name} is empty; a recording is a header and its events")
191	    header = RecordingHeader.model_validate_json(written[0])
192	    lines: list[tuple[str, dict[str, Any]]] = []
193	    for line in written[1:]:
194	        said = json.loads(line)
195	        lines.append((str(said["event"]), dict(said["data"])))
196	    return Recording(example=path.stem, header=header, lines=tuple(lines))
197	
198	
199	def every_recording(folder: Path | None = None) -> tuple[Recording, ...]:
200	    """Read every recording in a folder, in a fixed order.
201	
202	    A folder with nothing in it gives nothing back, which is what lets the build's
203	    own check be green from the commit that adds it.
204	
205	    Args:
206	        folder: Where the recordings live. The committed folder when not said.
207	
208	    Returns:
209	        Every recording, by file name.
210	    """
211	    # Resolved when asked rather than when this function was written, so that
212	    # where the recordings live is a fact about the running program.
213	    looking_in = where_they_live() if folder is None else folder
214	    if not looking_in.is_dir():
215	        return ()
216	    return tuple(read(one) for one in sorted(looking_in.glob("*.jsonl")))
217	
218	
219	def summaries(folder: Path | None = None) -> tuple[RecordingSummary, ...]:
220	    """List what this copy of the program can play back, and when each was made.
221	
222	    Read by the first screen before anything runs, which is how the sentence
223	    record 0012 requires — *"No model key configured — these run from recordings
224	    made on <date>"* — can name a date at all: the date lives on the receipt, and
225	    the receipt arrives last.
226	
227	    Args:
228	        folder: Where the recordings live. The committed folder when not said.
229	
230	    Returns:
231	        One summary per recording, by file name.
232	    """
233	    return tuple(
234	        RecordingSummary(example=one.example, recording_date=one.header.recording_date)
235	        for one in every_recording(folder)
236	    )
237	
238	
239	def find(hypothesis: str, folder: Path | None = None) -> Recording | None:
240	    """Find the recording made from this sentence, or nothing at all.
241	
242	    **Matched on the sentence, exact after trimming surrounding spaces** — the
243	    same rule the scripted intervention uses, because one matching rule is easier
244	    to trust than two. Never a nearest match: playing one map back at somebody who
245	    asked about something else is worse than saying no, and afterwards it is
246	    indistinguishable from the product working.
247	
248	    Args:
249	        hypothesis: The sentence the person typed.
250	        folder: Where the recordings live. The committed folder when not said.
251	
252	    Returns:
253	        The one recording made from that sentence, or nothing at all.
254	    """
255	    wanted = hypothesis.strip()
256	    for one in every_recording(folder):
257	        if one.hypothesis.strip() == wanted:
258	            return one
259	    return None
260	
261	
262	def play(recording: Recording) -> Iterator[Event]:
263	    """Play one recording back as the events a live run would have emitted.
264	
265	    Every event comes straight out of the file except the receipt, which is
266	    rebuilt to say that this run made no calls. The likelihoods are not in the
267	    file at all: `beliefs_of` recomputes them, and whoever writes the bytes out
268	    puts that event where the grammar requires.
269	
270	    Args:
271	        recording: The recording to play.
272	
273	    Yields:
274	        The events, in the order the file holds them.
275	    """
276	    for name, payload in recording.lines:
277	        if name == events.NAMES[Receipt]:
278	            yield _rebuilt(payload, recording)
279	            continue
280	        yield events.BY_NAME[name].model_validate(payload)
281	
282	
283	def seconds_between(instant: bool | None = None) -> float:
284	    """How long to wait between two events of a replay.
285	
286	    Pacing is presentation and nothing else, which is why it is **not** a field on
287	    the request: a client that could ask for an instant replay would let anybody
288	    who opened the network tab skip the thing the recording exists to show. It is
289	    a setting, read here, and a caller may say so plainly instead.
290	
291	    Args:
292	        instant: True to drop the delay to nothing, or nothing at all to let the
293	            program's own settings decide.
294	
295	    Returns:
296	        The seconds to wait between events.
297	    """
298	    if instant is None:
299	        instant = get_settings().REPLAY_INSTANT
300	    return 0.0 if instant else A_COMFORTABLE_PACE
301	
302	
303	def beliefs_of(recording: Recording, world_sizes: tuple[int, int]) -> BeliefsPropagated:
304	    """Work every likelihood through the map this recording built.
305	
306	    The one event a recording never stores. The header carries the seed, the
307	    accepted proposals carry the map, and the rules layer does the rest — so a
308	    replay and a live run end up running the identical map, branch and seed
309	    through the identical arithmetic.
310	
311	    Args:
312	        recording: The recording whose map to work through.
313	        world_sizes: How many versions of the map to try, and how many worlds
314	            under each.
315	
316	    Returns:
317	        The event, ready to be written out where the grammar puts it.
318	    """
319	    versions, worlds = world_sizes
320	    world = propagate(
321	        map_of(recording),
322	        (),
323	        as_of=recording.header.recording_date,
324	        seed=recording.header.seed,
325	        versions=versions,
326	        worlds=worlds,
327	    )
328	    return BeliefsPropagated(world=world)
329	
330	
331	def map_of(recording: Recording) -> Graph:
332	    """Build the map this recording's accepted proposals left behind.
333	
334	    Nothing is minted here: every identifier in the file was minted when the
335	    recording was made, and reading them back is what makes a replayed map the
336	    same map.
337	
338	    Args:
339	        recording: The recording to read.
340	
341	    Returns:
342	        The finished map, with the header's identifier on it.
343	
344	    Raises:
345	        ValueError: If the recording holds no claim at all, which no committed
346	            file can.
347	    """
348	    claims: list[Proposition] = []
349	    arrows: list[Link] = []
350	    for name, payload in recording.lines:
351	        if name != events.NAMES[ProposalAccepted]:
352	            continue
353	        landed = ProposalAccepted.model_validate(payload)
354	        if landed.proposition is not None:
355	            claims.append(landed.proposition)
356	        arrows.extend(landed.links)
357	    if not claims:
358	        raise ValueError(f"{recording.example} holds no claim; there is no map to rebuild")
359	    return Graph(
360	        id=recording.header.base_id,
361	        propositions=tuple(claims),
362	        links=tuple(arrows),
363	        hypothesis_id=claims[0].id,
364	    )
365	
366	
367	def _rebuilt(recorded: dict[str, Any], recording: Recording) -> Receipt:
368	    """Rebuild a recorded receipt as the receipt of the replay that is running now.
369	
370	    Args:
371	        recorded: The receipt the original run emitted.
372	        recording: The recording it came from, for its header.
373	
374	    Returns:
375	        A receipt saying this run made no calls and cost nothing.
376	    """
377	    return Receipt(
378	        model=str(recorded.get("model", "")),
379	        calls=0,
380	        input_tokens=0,
381	        output_tokens=0,
382	        cache_read_tokens=0,
383	        searches=0,
384	        dollars=0.0,
385	        seconds=0.0,
386	        mode="replay",
387	        recording_date=recording.header.recording_date,
388	        prompt_hash=recording.header.prompt_hash,
389	    )
390	
391	
392	def faults_in(recording: Recording, *, current_prompt_hash: str) -> list[str]:
393	    """List everything wrong with one recording, in plain sentences.
394	
395	    What the build's own check reads. Every reason at once, never the first.
396	
397	    Args:
398	        recording: The recording to check.
399	        current_prompt_hash: The fingerprint of the prompt shipping today.
400	
401	    Returns:
402	        One sentence per fault, or nothing at all when the file is sound.
403	    """
404	    found: list[str] = []
405	    names = [name for name, _ in recording.lines]
406	
407	    unknown = sorted({one for one in names if one not in events.BY_NAME})
408	    if unknown:
409	        found.append(f"{recording.example} holds events nobody knows: {', '.join(unknown)}.")
410	    for name, payload in recording.lines:
411	        shape = events.BY_NAME.get(name)
412	        if shape is None:
413	            continue
414	        try:
415	            shape.model_validate(payload)
416	        except ValidationError:
417	            found.append(f"{recording.example} holds a {name} whose payload does not fit it.")
418	            break
419	
420	    if not names or names[0] != events.NAMES[GenerationStarted]:
421	        found.append(f"{recording.example} does not start where a generation starts.")
422	    if not names or names[-1] != events.NAMES[events.Done]:
423	        found.append(f"{recording.example} does not end where a generation ends.")
424	    if events.NAMES[BeliefsPropagated] in names:
425	        found.append(
426	            f"{recording.example} stores likelihoods. They are recomputed from the seed, "
427	            "so a stored one could disagree with the engine that is running."
428	        )
429	    if recording.header.prompt_hash != current_prompt_hash:
430	        found.append(
431	            f"{recording.example} was made against a different prompt from the one shipping "
432	            "today, so it shows wording this program no longer uses. Record it again."
433	        )
434	    return found
435

line carries exactly the two fields the wire carries, so the replayer writes them
straight out without re-deriving anything — which is what makes "a recording is
the stream, line for line" literally true rather than nearly true.

Two events are not re-emitted from the file
--------------------------------------------
**The receipt is rebuilt.** A replay made no calls, so it says exactly that: zero
calls, zero tokens, zero searches, zero dollars, the header's date and prompt
fingerprint, and `mode: "replay"`. The whole tally is zeroed together rather than
the dollars alone — a receipt showing tokens with no dollars would contradict its
own price table. The model is copied from the recorded receipt, because the
reader is entitled to know which model wrote this map, and the seconds are this
replay's own clock.

**The likelihoods are recomputed, and therefore never stored.** The header
carries the seed, the accepted proposals carry the map, and the rules layer does
the rest. So a recording holds no world at all: the files stay small, and replay
and live agree by construction rather than by care. Store the numbers instead and
the day propagation changes, the demo shows numbers the engine no longer
produces and nothing goes red.

What this file must never do
----------------------------
- Never write a recording. `make record-demo` is the only writer, and a
  hand-edited file is a piece of state that traces to nobody.
- Never guess which recording to play. The match is the person's own sentence,
  exact after trimming — playing the Hormuz map back at somebody who asked about
  photonic chips is worse than saying no, and afterwards it is indistinguishable
  from the product working.
- Never let the pacing change an event, an order or a number. It is cosmetic.
- Never honour a seed from the request. The header's seed is the one the recorded
  run had, and the numbers are recomputed from it.

RECORDINGS = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / "recordings"
"""Where the committed recordings live when nothing says otherwise.

`backend/recordings/`. The settings can point somewhere else — which is what lets
a test, and the one browser test that drives both halves, run against a folder of
their own without touching the committed one.
"""


def where_they_live() -> Path:
    """Where this running program reads its recordings from.

    Read when asked rather than when this module was written, so that pointing a
    program at another folder is a setting and not a patch.

    Returns:
        The folder, from the settings when they name one and `backend/recordings/`
        when they do not.
    """
    said = get_settings().KATALYST_RECORDINGS
    return Path(said) if said else RECORDINGS


A_COMFORTABLE_PACE = 0.6
"""Seconds between events when a recording is played at human speed.

Cosmetic and nothing else: it never changes an event, an order or a number. The
figure is chosen against a measurement rather than taste — a live proposal took
about a minute to come back on the first five recorded calls, so a replay that
raced would teach a reviewer that the product is faster than it is, and one that
matched would be unwatchable. This is the slowest speed somebody will sit through
and the fastest that still reads as *arriving* rather than *appearing*.
"""


class RecordedInsert(BaseModel):
    """The single scripted "…but X happens" a keyless reviewer can make on this map."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    claim_in_words: str = Field(description="What the card offers, word for word.")
    answer: Insert = Field(
        description="The claim and its arrows, drafted live when the recording was made."
    )


class RecordingHeader(BaseModel):
    """The first line of a recording: everything that is true of the whole file.

    It must never carry a likelihood, a range or a world. Numbers are recomputed
    from the seed, and a number stored here could one day disagree with the engine
    that is running.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    base_id: str = Field(
        description=(
            "The identifier of the map this recording builds, minted when the "
            "recording was made. Emphatically not the word `hormuz`: the file is "
            "named for the launchpad card, and the map inside carries a minted "
            "identifier so it can never be confused with the hand-written stored "
            "example that already answers to that name."
        )
    )
    seed: int = Field(description="The one number the rules layer re-propagates with.")
    recording_date: date = Field(description="The day `make record-demo` wrote this file.")
    prompt_hash: str = Field(description="The fingerprint of the prompt the run was made against.")
    insert: RecordedInsert = Field(
        description="The one scripted intervention this recording can answer."
    )


class RecordingSummary(BaseModel):
    """One recording the first screen can offer, and when it was made."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    example: str = Field(description="The short name of the example, matching its file name.")
    recording_date: date = Field(description="The day `make record-demo` wrote it.")


class Recording(BaseModel):
    """One whole recorded generation: its header and its events, in order."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    example: str = Field(description="The short name of the example, from the file's own name.")
    header: RecordingHeader = Field(description="Everything true of the whole file.")
    lines: tuple[tuple[str, dict[str, Any]], ...] = Field(
        description="Every event after the header, as the name it travels under and its payload."
    )

    @property
    def hypothesis(self) -> str:
        """The sentence this recording was made from, read off its own first event."""
        for name, payload in self.lines:
            if name == events.NAMES[GenerationStarted]:
                return str(payload.get("hypothesis", ""))
        return ""


def read(path: Path) -> Recording:
    """Read one recording off disk.

    Args:
        path: The file to read.

    Returns:
        Its header and its events, in the order they were written.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the file is empty, or its first line is not a header.
    """
    written = [one for one in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines() if one.strip()]
    if not written:
        raise ValueError(f"{path.name} is empty; a recording is a header and its events")
    header = RecordingHeader.model_validate_json(written[0])
    lines: list[tuple[str, dict[str, Any]]] = []
    for line in written[1:]:
        said = json.loads(line)
        lines.append((str(said["event"]), dict(said["data"])))
    return Recording(example=path.stem, header=header, lines=tuple(lines))


def every_recording(folder: Path | None = None) -> tuple[Recording, ...]:
    """Read every recording in a folder, in a fixed order.

    A folder with nothing in it gives nothing back, which is what lets the build's
    own check be green from the commit that adds it.

    Args:
        folder: Where the recordings live. The committed folder when not said.

    Returns:
        Every recording, by file name.
    """
    # Resolved when asked rather than when this function was written, so that
    # where the recordings live is a fact about the running program.
    looking_in = where_they_live() if folder is None else folder
    if not looking_in.is_dir():
        return ()
    return tuple(read(one) for one in sorted(looking_in.glob("*.jsonl")))


def summaries(folder: Path | None = None) -> tuple[RecordingSummary, ...]:
    """List what this copy of the program can play back, and when each was made.

    Read by the first screen before anything runs, which is how the sentence
    record 0012 requires — *"No model key configured — these run from recordings
    made on <date>"* — can name a date at all: the date lives on the receipt, and
    the receipt arrives last.

    Args:
        folder: Where the recordings live. The committed folder when not said.

    Returns:
        One summary per recording, by file name.
    """
    return tuple(
        RecordingSummary(example=one.example, recording_date=one.header.recording_date)
        for one in every_recording(folder)
    )


def find(hypothesis: str, folder: Path | None = None) -> Recording | None:
    """Find the recording made from this sentence, or nothing at all.

    **Matched on the sentence, exact after trimming surrounding spaces** — the
    same rule the scripted intervention uses, because one matching rule is easier
    to trust than two. Never a nearest match: playing one map back at somebody who
    asked about something else is worse than saying no, and afterwards it is
    indistinguishable from the product working.

    Args:
        hypothesis: The sentence the person typed.
        folder: Where the recordings live. The committed folder when not said.

    Returns:
        The one recording made from that sentence, or nothing at all.
    """
    wanted = hypothesis.strip()
    for one in every_recording(folder):
        if one.hypothesis.strip() == wanted:
            return one
    return None


def play(recording: Recording) -> Iterator[Event]:
    """Play one recording back as the events a live run would have emitted.

    Every event comes straight out of the file except the receipt, which is
    rebuilt to say that this run made no calls. The likelihoods are not in the
    file at all: `beliefs_of` recomputes them, and whoever writes the bytes out
    puts that event where the grammar requires.

    Args:
        recording: The recording to play.

    Yields:
        The events, in the order the file holds them.
    """
    for name, payload in recording.lines:
        if name == events.NAMES[Receipt]:
            yield _rebuilt(payload, recording)
            continue
        yield events.BY_NAME[name].model_validate(payload)


def seconds_between(instant: bool | None = None) -> float:
    """How long to wait between two events of a replay.

    Pacing is presentation and nothing else, which is why it is **not** a field on
    the request: a client that could ask for an instant replay would let anybody
    who opened the network tab skip the thing the recording exists to show. It is
    a setting, read here, and a caller may say so plainly instead.

    Args:
        instant: True to drop the delay to nothing, or nothing at all to let the
            program's own settings decide.

    Returns:
        The seconds to wait between events.
    """
    if instant is None:
        instant = get_settings().REPLAY_INSTANT
    return 0.0 if instant else A_COMFORTABLE_PACE


def beliefs_of(recording: Recording, world_sizes: tuple[int, int]) -> BeliefsPropagated:
    """Work every likelihood through the map this recording built.

    The one event a recording never stores. The header carries the seed, the
    accepted proposals carry the map, and the rules layer does the rest — so a
    replay and a live run end up running the identical map, branch and seed
    through the identical arithmetic.

    Args:
        recording: The recording whose map to work through.
        world_sizes: How many versions of the map to try, and how many worlds
            under each.

    Returns:
        The event, ready to be written out where the grammar puts it.
    """
    versions, worlds = world_sizes
    world = propagate(
        map_of(recording),
        (),
        as_of=recording.header.recording_date,
        seed=recording.header.seed,
        versions=versions,
        worlds=worlds,
    )
    return BeliefsPropagated(world=world)


def map_of(recording: Recording) -> Graph:
    """Build the map this recording's accepted proposals left behind.

    Nothing is minted here: every identifier in the file was minted when the
    recording was made, and reading them back is what makes a replayed map the
    same map.

    Args:
        recording: The recording to read.

    Returns:
        The finished map, with the header's identifier on it.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the recording holds no claim at all, which no committed
            file can.
    """
    claims: list[Proposition] = []
    arrows: list[Link] = []
    for name, payload in recording.lines:
        if name != events.NAMES[ProposalAccepted]:
            continue
        landed = ProposalAccepted.model_validate(payload)
        if landed.proposition is not None:
            claims.append(landed.proposition)
        arrows.extend(landed.links)
    if not claims:
        raise ValueError(f"{recording.example} holds no claim; there is no map to rebuild")
    return Graph(
        id=recording.header.base_id,
        propositions=tuple(claims),
        links=tuple(arrows),
        hypothesis_id=claims[0].id,
    )


def _rebuilt(recorded: dict[str, Any], recording: Recording) -> Receipt:
    """Rebuild a recorded receipt as the receipt of the replay that is running now.

    Args:
        recorded: The receipt the original run emitted.
        recording: The recording it came from, for its header.

    Returns:
        A receipt saying this run made no calls and cost nothing.
    """
    return Receipt(
        model=str(recorded.get("model", "")),
        calls=0,
        input_tokens=0,
        output_tokens=0,
        cache_read_tokens=0,
        searches=0,
        dollars=0.0,
        seconds=0.0,
        mode="replay",
        recording_date=recording.header.recording_date,
        prompt_hash=recording.header.prompt_hash,
    )


def faults_in(recording: Recording, *, current_prompt_hash: str) -> list[str]:
    """List everything wrong with one recording, in plain sentences.

    What the build's own check reads. Every reason at once, never the first.

    Args:
        recording: The recording to check.
        current_prompt_hash: The fingerprint of the prompt shipping today.

    Returns:
        One sentence per fault, or nothing at all when the file is sound.
    """
    found: list[str] = []
    names = [name for name, _ in recording.lines]

    unknown = sorted({one for one in names if one not in events.BY_NAME})
    if unknown:
        found.append(f"{recording.example} holds events nobody knows: {', '.join(unknown)}.")
    for name, payload in recording.lines:
        shape = events.BY_NAME.get(name)
        if shape is None:
            continue
        try:
            shape.model_validate(payload)
        except ValidationError:
            found.append(f"{recording.example} holds a {name} whose payload does not fit it.")
            break

    if not names or names[0] != events.NAMES[GenerationStarted]:
        found.append(f"{recording.example} does not start where a generation starts.")
    if not names or names[-1] != events.NAMES[events.Done]:
        found.append(f"{recording.example} does not end where a generation ends.")
    if events.NAMES[BeliefsPropagated] in names:
        found.append(
            f"{recording.example} stores likelihoods. They are recomputed from the seed, "
            "so a stored one could disagree with the engine that is running."
        )
    if recording.header.prompt_hash != current_prompt_hash:
        found.append(
            f"{recording.example} was made against a different prompt from the one shipping "
            "today, so it shows wording this program no longer uses. Record it again."
        )
    return found

248	    This is the thing to make assertions about.
249	
250	    Args:
251	        shape: A shape an answer must fit.
252	
253	    Returns:
254	        The description as the service will receive it.
255	    """
256	    schema: dict[str, Any] = TypeAdapter(shape).json_schema()
257	    tidied: dict[str, Any] = transform_schema(schema)

261	class AnswerWeCouldNotRead(Exception):
262	    """The model wrote something that did not fit the shape the call asked for.
263

265	    complaint, so that nothing past this file has to know whose complaint it was.
266	    Its sentence is written for a person.
267	    """

269	    def __init__(self, why: str) -> None:
270	        """Hold the plain sentence of what went wrong."""
271	        super().__init__(why)
272	        self.why = why
273	
274	
275	HOW_LONG_TO_WAIT = 300.0
276	"""How long one request may take before it is given up on, in seconds.
277	
278	The library's own default is ten minutes. Measured on 2026-09-17 and again on
279	2026-09-20, a whole question — every round of research it takes — runs about two
280	hundred seconds, and one round of it is well inside that. Ten minutes is
281	therefore not a timeout, it is a hang: three attempts of it is half an hour of
282	somebody watching a stream that will never move. Five minutes is comfortably
283	above anything measured and bounds a whole question, retries and all, at fifteen.
284	"""
285	
286	HOW_OFTEN_TO_TRY_AGAIN = 2
287	"""How many times the library tries a failed request again by itself.
288	
289	The library's own default, written down rather than inherited. It retries 408,
290	409, 429, every 5xx and every connection failure, with a wait between — which is
291	exactly the set of failures that go away on their own, and exactly the set this
292	program has no better answer to. A failed request is not billed, so trying again
293	is free; what it costs is time, which the figure above bounds.
294	"""

297	class TheModelDidNotAnswer(Exception):
298	    """The service could not be reached, or would not answer, after the library gave up.
299	
300	    The vendor's own exception classes stop here, as `AnswerWeCouldNotRead` stops
301	    the library's validation errors here: nothing past this file knows whose
302	    complaint it was. Carries one plain sentence a person could read.
303	    """

306	        """Hold the plain sentence of what went wrong."""

311	def _in_plain_words(failure: anthropic.APIError) -> str:
312	    """Say what went wrong with a call, in words a person reads.
313	
314	    Never the exception's class, never a status code, never a stack trace: those
315	    belong in the server's own log. What a reader needs is whether to wait, to
316	    try a smaller run, or to tell somebody.
317	
318	    Args:
319	        failure: Whatever the library raised.
320	
321	    Returns:
322	        One plain sentence.
323	    """
324	    if isinstance(failure, anthropic.APITimeoutError):
325	        return "The model did not answer in time, twice over, so this question was given up on."
326	    if isinstance(failure, anthropic.APIConnectionError):
327	        return "The model could not be reached. The connection failed, twice over."
328	    if isinstance(failure, anthropic.RateLimitError):
329	        return "This run has asked too much of the model too quickly, and was turned away."
330	    if isinstance(failure, anthropic.APIStatusError) and failure.status_code >= 500:
331	        return "The model is busy and turned this question away, twice over."
332	    if isinstance(failure, anthropic.APIStatusError) and failure.status_code in (401, 403):
333	        return "The key this run was started with is not allowed to ask this model."
334	    if isinstance(failure, anthropic.APIStatusError) and failure.status_code == 402:

339	class Answerer(Protocol):
340	    """Whatever the pipeline asks its questions of.
341	
342	    Two questions, because a run asks two kinds. Before anything is expanded, a
343	    sentence a person typed is turned into a claim anybody could settle. After
344	    that, every call asks for the one next piece of the map.
345	
346	    Both hand back one `Said`. A question that came back part finished and was
347	    sent back to be continued is still one answer; every trip it took is on its
348	    counters, and a bill that quietly missed one would make the spending cap a
349	    lie.
350	
351	    Both raise `AnswerWeCouldNotRead` when the model wrote something that did not
352	    fit the shape.
353	    """
354	
355	    def watching(self, spent: Receipt, cap: float) -> None:
356	        """Say what the run has spent and what it may spend, before the next question.
357	
358	        Called before every question. An answerer that cannot go over a budget —
359	        every fake in the tests — may do nothing with it.
360	        """
361	        ...
362	
363	    def starting_claim(self, question: str, *, may_search: bool = True) -> Said:
364	        """Ask for one typed sentence, written as a claim anybody could settle."""
365	        ...
366	
367	    def proposal(self, question: str, *, may_search: bool) -> Said:
368	        """Ask for the one next piece of the map, searching or not."""
369	        ...

372	class Model:
373	    """The live answerer: the vendor's own client, and nothing added to it.
374	
375	    Built around an already-made client so that a caller can hand in one with a
376	    different patience or a different address without this file growing a second
377	    way to be configured.
378	
379	    This class must never look at what was *said*. It asks, it sends a
380	    part-finished answer back to be continued, and it translates. Reading an
381	    answer — accepting it, refusing it, saying it made no sense — belongs to
382	    `expand.py`, which can be tested without spending a penny.
383	    """
384	
385	    def __init__(
386	        self,
387	        client: anthropic.Anthropic,
388	        *,
389	        model: str | None = None,
390	        effort: str | None = None,
391	    ) -> None:
392	        """Wrap a client.
393	
394	        Args:
395	            client: The vendor's client, already built and already holding
396	                whatever credentials it needs.
397	            model: Which model to ask. The one the settings name when not said.
398	            effort: How hard it should try. The one the settings name when not
399	                said, and nothing at all when neither says — which leaves the
400	                service's own default and puts no field in the request.
401	        """
402	        self._client = client
403	        settings = get_settings()
404	        self._model = model or settings.KATALYST_MODEL
405	        chosen: Any = effort if effort is not None else settings.KATALYST_EFFORT
406	        # Pinned for the whole run and never varied between calls: changing it
407	        # mid-run would throw away the remembered prefix the run is reading back
408	        # at a tenth of the price. Left empty it is not sent at all, so the
409	        # request is byte for byte what it was before anybody had an opinion.
410	        self._trying: OutputConfigParam | Omit = (
411	            OutputConfigParam(effort=chosen) if chosen else omit
412	        )
413	        self._spent = nothing_spent_yet(self._model)
414	        self._cap = float("inf")
415	        self.waits_for = getattr(client, "timeout", None)
416	        self.tries_again = getattr(client, "max_retries", None)
417	
418	    def watching(self, spent: Receipt, cap: float) -> None:
419	        """Take note of what the run has spent and what it may spend.
420	
421	        Args:
422	            spent: What the run had spent before this question was put.
423	            cap: What the whole run may spend, in dollars.
424	        """
425	        self._spent = spent
426	        self._cap = cap
427	
428	    def starting_claim(self, question: str, *, may_search: bool = True) -> Said:
429	        """Ask for one typed sentence, written as a claim anybody could settle.
430	
431	        **Searching is allowed here**, which it was not at first. The question is
432	        partly what the person meant, which the web has nothing to say about — and
433	        partly how often this kind of thing has happened before, which is exactly
434	        what the web is for. The first claim of a map is the one every number
435	        below it hangs off, and it was the one claim nobody could look anything up
436	        for.
437	
438	        Args:
439	            question: The varying half of the request, from `prompt.py`.
440	            may_search: Whether this run still has searches left.
441	
442	        Returns:
443	            The answer, in our own words.
444	        """
445	        return self._ask(question, StartingClaim, may_search=may_search)
446	
447	    def proposal(self, question: str, *, may_search: bool) -> Said:
448	        """Ask for the one next piece of the map.
449	
450	        Args:
451	            question: The varying half of the request, from `prompt.py`.
452	            may_search: Whether this run still has searches left. False forbids
453	                the tool for this call and leaves it in the list.
454	
455	        Returns:
456	            The answer, in our own words.
457	        """
458	        return self._ask(question, OneProposal, may_search=may_search)
459	
460	    def _ask(self, question: str, shape: Any, *, may_search: bool) -> Said:
461	        """Put one question, sending a part-finished answer back until it finishes.
462	
463	        The shape is handed to the client library, which turns it into the
464	        description of what an answer must look like, sends it with the request,
465	        and checks what comes back against it before returning.
466	
467	        The shape goes on `output_format`, which is what `messages.parse` takes;
468	        the reference bundle's note that `output_format` is deprecated is about
469	        `messages.create`, where the same thing is spelled `output_config.format`.
470	        `messages.parse` merges the two itself. Do not "fix" this to the other
471	        spelling — decision record 0006 names this call.
472	
473	        Args:
474	            question: The varying half of the request.
475	            shape: What an answer must fit — a starting claim, or a proposal.
476	            may_search: Whether the search tool may be used on this call.
477	
478	        Returns:
479	            The answer, in our own words.
480	
481	        Raises:
482	            AnswerWeCouldNotRead: If what came back did not fit the shape.
483	            TheModelDidNotAnswer: If the service could not be reached, or would
484	                not answer, after the library had tried again as often as it may.
485	        """
486	        conversation: list[MessageParam] = [{"role": "user", "content": question}]
487	        rounds: list[ParsedMessage[Any]] = []
488	        started = time.monotonic()
489	        for _ in range(ROUNDS_OF_RESEARCH):
490	            try:
491	                answer = self._client.messages.parse(
492	                    model=self._model,
493	                    max_tokens=ROOM_FOR_AN_ANSWER,
494	                    # The model decides for itself how long to think. How hard it
495	                    # tries is left at the service's own default, which is the
496	                    # setting we want; naming it would add a knob that changes
497	                    # nothing and a second place for two settings to disagree.
498	                    thinking={"type": "adaptive"},
499	                    system=STANDING_BLOCK,
500	                    tools=[SEARCH_TOOL],
501	                    tool_choice=MAY_SEARCH if may_search else MAY_NOT_SEARCH,
502	                    messages=conversation,
503	                    output_format=shape,
504	                    output_config=self._trying,
505	                )
506	            except ValidationError as did_not_fit:
507	                raise AnswerWeCouldNotRead(_did_not_fit_the_shape(did_not_fit)) from did_not_fit
508	            except anthropic.APIError as did_not_answer:
509	                # Everything the library raises stops here. The pipeline folds a
510	                # sentence, never an exception class (Kent, 2026-09-20).
511	                raise TheModelDidNotAnswer(_in_plain_words(did_not_answer)) from did_not_answer
512	            rounds.append(answer)
513	            if answer.stop_reason != "pause_turn":
514	                return what_it_said(rounds, seconds=time.monotonic() - started)
515	            if self._out_of_money(rounds):
516	                # The rounds already paid for are kept and read as they stand.
517	                return what_it_said(rounds, seconds=time.monotonic() - started)
518	            # Part finished. The service picks up from its own turn, and adding a
519	            # "carry on" of our own would only confuse it.
520	            conversation = [*conversation, {"role": "assistant", "content": answer.content}]

522	
523	    def _out_of_money(self, rounds: Sequence[ParsedMessage[Any]]) -> bool:
524	        """Say whether the rounds so far have taken the run past what it may spend.
525	
526	        Priced through the same receipt the run itself is priced through, so the
527	        figure that stops a question mid-flight and the figure on the bill are
528	        worked out by one piece of code.
529	
530	        Args:
531	            rounds: Every round trip this question has made so far.
532	
533	        Returns:
534	            True once this question's rounds have carried the run over its cap.
535	        """
536	        return over_the_cap(fold(self._spent, what_it_said(rounds)), self._cap)

539	def what_it_said(rounds: Sequence[ParsedMessage[Any]], *, seconds: float = 0.0) -> Said:
540	    """Turn every round trip of one question into one answer in our own words.
541	
542	    The only place a reply of the library's becomes a shape of ours. Pure: it
543	    reads what it is given and asks nothing of anybody, which is what lets the
544	    tests put hand-written replies through the very same translation a live call
545	    goes through.
546	
547	    What the model wrote and what the search returned come out in **two different
548	    fields**, because the whole grounding rule rests on never confusing them.
549	
550	    A proposal arrives inside the envelope the wire forced on it, and leaves
551	    without one.
552	
553	    Args:
554	        rounds: Every round trip the question took, oldest first. The last one
555	            holds the answer.
556	        seconds: How long the whole question took, measured by the caller that
557	            made it. Passed in rather than read here, so this stays a pure
558	            function of an answer and a test can hand it a fixed number.
559	
560	    Returns:
561	        The answer, its search results, whether the model declined, and the sum of
562	        what every trip cost.
563	    """
564	    last = rounds[-1]
565	    answered = last.parsed_output
566	    if isinstance(answered, OneProposal):
567	        # The envelope comes off here, so nothing past this file ever sees it.
568	        answered = answered.proposal
569	    return Said(
570	        answered=answered,
571	        found=_pages_the_search_returned(rounds),
572	        declined=_declined(last),
573	        calls=len(rounds),
574	        searches=sum(
575	            one.usage.server_tool_use.web_search_requests if one.usage.server_tool_use else 0
576	            for one in rounds
577	        ),
578	        input_tokens=sum(one.usage.input_tokens for one in rounds),
579	        output_tokens=sum(one.usage.output_tokens for one in rounds),
580	        cache_read_tokens=sum(one.usage.cache_read_input_tokens or 0 for one in rounds),
581	        cache_write_tokens=sum(one.usage.cache_creation_input_tokens or 0 for one in rounds),
582	        thinking_tokens=sum(
583	            one.usage.output_tokens_details.thinking_tokens
584	            if one.usage.output_tokens_details
585	            else 0
586	            for one in rounds
587	        ),
588	        seconds=seconds,
589	    )

591	
592	def _pages_the_search_returned(rounds: Sequence[ParsedMessage[Any]]) -> tuple[FoundPage, ...]:
593	    """Read the search tool's own results out of an answer, and nothing else.
594	
595	    A question sent back to be continued can search on either trip, so the results
596	    are the whole question's rather than the last trip's. A page returned twice is
597	    kept once, in the order it first arrived.
598	
599	    A search that failed comes back as one error object where a list of results
600	    would be, which reads here as nothing found.
601	
602	    Args:
603	        rounds: Every round trip the question took, oldest first.
604	
605	    Returns:
606	        One page per result, in the order the tool returned them.
607	    """
608	    found: list[FoundPage] = []
609	    seen: set[str] = set()
610	    for one in rounds:
611	        for block in one.content:
612	            if block.type != "web_search_tool_result":
613	                continue
614	            results = block.content
615	            if not isinstance(results, list):
616	                continue  # The tool reported an error instead of results.
617	            for result in results:
618	                if result.type != "web_search_result" or result.url in seen:
619	                    continue
620	                seen.add(result.url)
621	                found.append(FoundPage(url=result.url, title=result.title))
622	    return tuple(found)
623	
624	
625	def _declined(answer: ParsedMessage[Any]) -> str | None:
626	    """Say, in plain words, that the model declined the question — or that it did not.
627	
628	    The vendor's own safety check can turn a call down. That comes back as an
629	    ordinary answer with a stop reason saying so, and sometimes with an
630	    explanation. It is surfaced as a refusal a person sees, never hidden and never
631	    quietly re-routed to a different model — decision record 0006 declines the
632	    server-side rerouting the reference bundle offers, for exactly that reason.
633	
634	    Args:
635	        answer: The last round trip's answer.
636	
637	    Returns:
638	        One plain sentence, or nothing at all when the model did not decline.
639	    """
640	    if answer.stop_reason != "refusal":
641	        return None
642	    details = answer.stop_details
643	    if details is not None and details.explanation:
644	        return f"The model declined to answer this question. It said: {details.explanation}"
645	    return "The model declined to answer this question."
646	
647	
648	def _did_not_fit_the_shape(problem: ValidationError) -> str:
649	    """Say, in plain words, that the answer did not fit the shape we asked for.
650	
651	    Nothing technical reaches a screen. The field names are the same words this
652	    spec uses for those fields, so naming them helps rather than mystifies.
653	
654	    Args:
655	        problem: What the shape check objected to.
656	
657	    Returns:
658	        One plain sentence.
659	    """
660	    fields = sorted(
661	        {
662	            ".".join(str(step) for step in fault["loc"] if not str(step).startswith("function-"))
663	            for fault in problem.errors()
664	        }
665	    )
666	    named = ", ".join(field for field in fields if field)
667	    if not named:
668	        return "The model's answer did not fit the shape this call asked for."
669	    return f"The model's answer did not fit the shape this call asked for, at: {named}."
670	
671	
672	def _named(path: str) -> Any:
673	    """Build whatever `module:name` names, by calling it.
674	
675	    Args:
676	        path: An import path of the form `module:name`, naming something that
677	            can be called with no arguments and hands back an answerer.
678	
679	    Returns:
680	        Whatever that factory built.
681	
682	    Raises:
683	        ValueError: If the path does not name a module and something in it.
684	    """
685	    module, _, name = path.partition(":")
686	    if not module or not name:
687	        raise ValueError(
688	            f"KATALYST_ANSWERER is {path!r}, which does not name anything. It wants "
689	            "'module:name', where the name can be called with no arguments."
690	        )
691	    return getattr(import_module(module), name)()
692	
693	
694	def live_answerer(*, effort: str | None = None) -> Model | None:
695	    """Build the live answerer, or say plainly that there is no key for one.
696	
697	    The one function that knows whether this program can call a model at all.
698	    Nothing here raises and nothing here prints: a missing key is an ordinary fact
699	    about how the program was started, and the screen says so rather than failing.
700	
701	    Args:
702	        effort: How hard the model should try on this run, when a measurement run
703	            has said. The settings decide when it has not.
704	
705	    Returns:
706	        A live answerer, or nothing at all when no key is configured.
707	    """
708	    stand_in = get_settings().KATALYST_ANSWERER
709	    if stand_in:
710	        # The one seam that lets the recorder be started as a program in a test,
711	        # with no key and no network. Empty everywhere but there, and a run
712	        # answered this way can never become a recording — `record.py` names it
713	        # as a fault (Kent, 2026-09-20).
714	        return _named(stand_in)
715	    key = get_settings().ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
716	    if not key:
717	        return None
718	    return Model(
719	        anthropic.Anthropic(
720	            api_key=key,
721	            timeout=HOW_LONG_TO_WAIT,
722	            max_retries=HOW_OFTEN_TO_TRY_AGAIN,
723	        ),
724	        effort=effort,
725	    )
